versions.changelog: Security: the data-fetch host allowlist is now rechecked on every redirect hop. It previously validated only the initial URL while urlopen followed redirects, so a redirect could leave the declared network.

Security: the declared egress allowlist is now enforced on data fetches too, not just webhook delivery — an arbitrary URL could previously be fetched, including internal and cloud-metadata addresses. Docs: references/config.md still described monitoring as auto-enabling and lacked the warnings about what a webhook sends and that scheduling modifies your system.

Fix: schedule status treated any OpenClaw cron job named with 'SignalRadar' as this skill's own — the delete path was fixed last release, the status path was not. Docs: the protocol reference still claimed the reply route persists indefinitely and that onboarding enables monitoring; both stopped being true earlier. The scheduler prompt no longer dictates the agent's reply format.

Security: refuse plain-HTTP webhook delivery. The webhook URL is a bearer credential and the alert body carries what you monitor, so http:// is now rejected at both the delivery and config entry points; SIGNALRADAR_ALLOW_INSECURE_WEBHOOK=1 opts back in.

Docs: every description of the scheduling behaviour now matches the code — Quick Start, the Scheduling section and the configuration table still described the pre-1.5.0 auto-start behaviour and the old Asia/Shanghai timezone default

Fix: schedule disable deleted OpenClaw cron jobs whose name merely contained 'SignalRadar', including jobs the user created; deletion now requires an exact name match. The reply-route file is written only when openclaw is the configured delivery channel, instead of on any invocation whose environment carried those variables.

Security: pin webhook connections to the validated address (DNS-rebinding resistant, proxy-aware, certificate verification unchanged); scope the file adapter to the data directory; expire the stored reply route after 30 days with a clear-route command; timezone follows the machine instead of a hardcoded zone; add a machine-readable metadata.permissions declaration
Security: remove the unconditional runtime-host assertion (the skill no longer tells the agent which platform it is on; it reads the configured delivery channel instead)

Security: ask before installing the background scheduler (schedule.auto_enable now defaults to ask; --yes keeps the unattended path for automation); CR-12 describes agent-directed text instead of quoting payload examples, which had itself tripped the prompt-injection detector
Security: credential masking on every output path, SSRF + redirect guards, narrowed allowed-tools, schedule.auto_enable opt-out; fixes 'config delivery webhook <url>' failing without quotes
Add read-only market discovery: `discover` CLI command (keyword search + trending browse) and `discover_markets` MCP tool. Results feed the existing add flow — never auto-adds, never scheduled.

Packaging/security fix: the optional MCP server (skills/signalradar/mcp/) is now excluded from the ClawHub package via .clawhubignore, so the published skill stays zero-dependency / stdlib-only (matches requires.pip:[]). The MCP server remains available via GitHub clone (see mcp/README.md). The prepublish gate now blocks shipping any dependency manifest when the skill declares zero-dep, preventing this class of declared-vs-actual contradiction. Also corrected an internal HIT JSON doc example to percentage-scale probabilities. No changes to monitoring, thresholds, scheduling, or delivery behavior.

HIT alerts now include display-only context lines: directional 7-day price trend (from CLOB price-history, fetched only when an alert fires) and 24h volume/liquidity (no extra requests). New config source.trend_context (default true); set false to restore minimal alerts. Copy refinements: target-emoji prefix on the change line, money emoji for volume/liquidity, blank line before the footer in all pushes, digest separators removed and digest header spacing improved for mobile. No changes to thresholds, baselines, or scheduling.
